data.cultural_impact: The name Shurayh carries a significant cultural impact in the Muslim community, derivatives of this name have been used in various historical and literary works over the centuries. Historically, there has been a notable figure named Umar bin Al-Khattab Al-Shurayh bin Hafs, who was a companion of Prophet Muhammad and became the second Caliph of the Rashidun Caliphate. He is respected and renowned for his unwavering commitment to Islam and his military prowess in protecting and expanding the Muslim community.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Shurayh holds immense spiritual significance for Muslims, as it represents the concept of protection, defence, and shielding. In Islamic theology, Allah (God) is considered the greatest shield and protector, and Muslims believe in seeking His protection through various means such as prayer and acts of righteousness. The name also emphasizes the importance of protecting one's faith, family, and community, and follows the model set by Prophet Muhammad, as well as historical figures like Umar bin Al-Khattab, who demonstrated a strong commitment to shielding Islam and their communities from harm.

historical_references.context: Shurayh ibn Hani' Al-Khuza'i was a notable poet from the pre-Islamic Arab tribe of Khuza'a. He is renowned for composing elegies on the death of his father, Hani ibn Rabi'ah. These poems were later set to music and sung as mourning songs during weddings and other festive occasions.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Hazm, Al-Jamhwa wa Al-'Ulaf, p. 121. The name Shurayh carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Shurayh ibn Hani' Al-Qushayri was a scholar and poet from the Qushayr tribe. He wrote a work on Sufism and mysticism, Ihya' Ulum Al-Din, which became a major influence in the development of Sufi thought.
